first.rationale: Two inherited findings directly support onboarding simplification, which addresses the current completion decline and has previously produced durable activation and time-to-value gains. Verify both records to confirm downstream qualified-revenue evidence and experiment applicability before committing; avoid promotional pricing because its known retention harm conflicts with sustainable growth.

final.rationale: Run a standard guarded experiment shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction, prioritizing SMB self-serve accounts. This directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion decline and may also recover activation. The strongest record improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention; the SMB record improved signup, activation, and qualified revenue. Monitor retention closely because the SMB result included a 1% decline, and do not extrapolate beyond SMB without evidence. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its known material retention harm conflicts with sustainable long-term qualified revenue.
